questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why bats appear in so many superhero films
How to protect your home from bats
The complicated relationship between humans and bats
How farmers grow crops without insects
questions.why: Neil says the relationship is complex and asks whether we should think of bats as friend or enemy.

questions.q: What interesting bat fact does Sam give?
options: All bats eat fruit
About one in five mammal species is a bat
Bats only live in dark places
Most bats have two-metre wingspans
questions.why: Sam says bats account for 1 in 5 of all mammal species.

questions.q: Why are medical scientists interested in bats?
options: To make new vaccines from their blood
To learn how they fly in the dark
To stop them spreading insects
To learn the secrets of their long lives
questions.why: Sam says scientists study them hoping to discover the secrets of their anti-ageing and long life.

questions.q: According to Dr Winifred Frick, how do bats help US farming?
options: They eat huge numbers of insect pests
They scare away larger animals
They improve the soil
They carry seeds to new fields
questions.why: She says bats provide billions of dollars to US agriculture by eating agricultural pest insects.

questions.q: What do almost all scientists agree about Covid-19?
options: It started in a laboratory
Its progenitor virus has already been found
Its ancestral virus came from bats
Bats caught it from humans
questions.why: Sam says 99% of scientists would agree the 'ancestral virus' of Covid-19 came from bats.

questions.q: What is Professor Linfa Wang trying to find?
options: The missing 'go-between' virus
A cure for Covid-19 that works on bats
A new species of bat in Singapore
A way to stop bats getting sick
questions.why: He calls finding the progenitor virus the 'holy grail' for Covid-19.

questions.q: According to Professor Wang, how similar must the progenitor virus be to the outbreak virus?
options: About 50% identical
99.9% identical
Exactly 100% identical
About 90% identical
questions.why: He says the progenitor virus usually has to be 99.9% identical to the outbreak virus.

questions.q: What is Sam's final view about bats?
options: They are dangerous and people should avoid them
They are only useful to farmers
They clearly caused the pandemic
They're unfairly blamed but helpful
questions.why: Sam says bats are sometimes wrongly blamed for Covid but are good friends to farmers and scientists.
